tei:titleStmt.tei:title: A Prayer for Game Day [Super Bowl LX], by Rabbi Menachem Creditor

tei:div.tei:head: A Prayer for Game Day [Super Bowl LX], by Rabbi Menachem Creditor

tei:lg.tei:l: Ribbono shel Olam,
On this day when many hearts beat in unison
and many voices practice the ancient art of hopeful shouting,
we thank You for the gift of community,
for strangers in the same colors becoming family for an afternoon.
As once a shepherd ran toward a giant
with courage larger than his equipment,
may our team play with heart, grit, and a touch of holy chutzpah.
As one ancestor wrestled through the night
and emerged changed,
may there be struggle that brings out blessing,
not injury, not bitterness.
Teach us, as our sages hinted,
that true strength is not only in muscle or speed
but in restraint, teamwork, and knowing when to pass the ball.
Let joy be loud, losses be humane,
and tomorrow’s conversations kind.
And when the final whistle sounds,
remind us to breathe, to rest,
and to remember that win or lose,
we are still on the same team
learning how to show up for one another.
Amen.
